title: Customer Journey Mapping for Small Business: A Simple Framework

facts.fact: Gladly's customer journey research reports that 61% of small businesses receive more than half their revenue from repeat customers.
facts.quote: Gladly's customer journey research reports that 61% of small businesses receive more than half their revenue from repeat customers.

facts.fact: According to Opiniator's analysis of customer journey mapping pitfalls, 68% of customers abandon a business due to perceived indifference.
facts.quote: 68% of customers abandon a business due to perceived indifference

facts.fact: According to Harvard Business School Online's customer journey map guidance, 67% of customer journey maps fail to drive organizational change because they are created as static artifacts without clear objectives.
facts.quote: 67% of customer journey maps fail to drive organizational change because they're created as static artifacts without clear objectives

facts.fact: The article recommends that local businesses use five stages for a customer journey map rather than fifteen.
According to a LinkedIn analysis cited by Adwave, 45% of local customers use TV ads as an initial awareness trigger but complete the journey via search or social media within 3 days.
facts.quote: 45% of local customers use TV ads as an initial awareness trigger but complete the journey via search or social media within 3 days

facts.fact: Adwave's guide defines Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) as the total revenue generated by a campaign divided by the campaign cost.
facts.quote: The formula is simple: divide the total revenue generated by the campaign cost.

facts.fact: An Adwave infographic on customer journey metrics covers four essential metrics: CAC, conversion rate, CLTV, and retention.
facts.quote: A visual infographic explaining four essential customer journey metrics for small business growth, including CAC, conversion rate, CLTV, and retention.
